story.title: Justice Department vs. California over alleged noncitizen ballots before the midterms
story.summary: The Justice Department says thousands of people it calls likely noncitizens were sent mail-in ballots in California. It demanded that Los Angeles County and the Secretary of State review a federal list within 48 hours, then sued them to block those votes from being counted; a court hearing is set for Tuesday. State officials say federal data is unreliable and that voter eligibility is the state's responsibility.

development.summary: On Friday, Oct 23, the Justice Department widened the push: letters to at least 18 California counties demanding they set aside and verify mail-in ballots of alleged noncitizens within 48 hours and hand over voter data, warning that officials who knowingly tabulate such ballots could face federal charges.

why_now: Escalation from one county to most of the state, with a criminal-liability warning to election officials, ten days before the Nov 3 midterms and days before the court hearing.
